subject: Pilot SLO exception & commercial construct — Nexori Systems
messages:
From: Katie O'Neal <katie.oneal@nexori.systems>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@nexori.systems>, Nexori Legal <legal@nexori.systems>
Date: 2027-05-20T15:14:00Z
Subject: Pilot ask — uptime tolerance and commercial framing

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team was impressed with the throughput and the integration path looks straightforward. We're ready to move forward with a three-month pilot for part of our user base, but we have a couple of constraints from Procurement and Security that I'd like to surface up-front so we can avoid rework: 

- Uptime tolerance: Procurement is asking that we operate the pilot under a relaxed uptime SLO of 99.8% (instead of the standard 99.95) for the initial 90 days due to observed variability with our traffic profile.
- Service credit structure: They want a clearly capped remedy for pilot months (we prefer a firm cap at 50% of monthly fees) in exchange for a deeper commercial concession.
- Commercial ask: To offset their perceived risk, Nexori is asking for a one-time pilot discount in the 25–35% range on hosting charges for the pilot period.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a temporary SLO deviation and the suggested remedy cap, and what commercial discount you could offer for the pilot? If we can agree quickly, Legal will send a short SOW and we can start onboarding the week of 6/7.

Attachments: Nexori-SOW-v2.pdf (stub)

Best,
Katie
Head of Partnerships, Nexori Systems
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Katie O'Neal <katie.oneal@nexori.systems>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@nexori.systems>
Date: 2027-05-20T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — uptime tolerance and commercial framing

Katie — really glad to hear the demo resonated. Short answer: we can get creative for a pilot, but I need to loop in Deal Desk and Ops to confirm risk and the right mitigations. Two quick data points:

- We have precedent for temporary SLO relaxations for pilots if we pair them with hard guardrails (short duration, rollback triggers, and telemetry commitments).
- Service credit caps are negotiable — we typically push to keep credits below 50% for new pilots; approval thresholds depend on discount depth and exec sign-off.

I'll pull together a commercial construct and loop in Marissa and Ben — aim to get you a proposal by EOD tomorrow. Appreciate the SOW stub; that will speed Legal review.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Nexori pilot — recommended commercial construct (requesting exec approval)

Team — I reviewed Nexori's ask and Nexus SOW. Recommended construct below for Deal Desk:

Summary proposal (Deal Desk recommended):
- Pilot term: 90 days (start triggered by SOW signature).
- Temporary uptime SLO: 99.8% for pilot months only.
- Remedy profile: capped service credits for pilot months. Recommended cap = 50% of monthly hosting fees.
- Commercial: 30% discount on hosting fees for the pilot period (single-line item; non-recurring).
- Non-standard guardrails: weekly SLA dashboard shared with Nexori, automated rollback if incident rate exceeds agreed threshold for two consecutive weeks, and direct access to our Priority Response channel during pilot.

Rationale: 30% addresses Nexori's risk while keeping their total potential recovery (credits) controlled via the cap. If execs will not approve a 50% cap, alternative ask would be to accept a 40% cap with a slightly reduced discount (25%).

Approval asks (please respond with exactly one of the three below):
A) Approve as-is (30% discount + 50% credit cap)
B) Approve conditional (30% discount + 40% credit cap) — Deal Desk will adjust paperwork to reflect 25% if cap lowered
C) Decline — take back to customer with Redwood standard SLO (99.95) and demo further mitigations

Attachments: redwood-uptime-exception-term-sheet.docx, discount-math.xlsx (stubs)

Jonas — requesting exec sign-off choice A or B. Please advise — Legal will need this direction for SOW redline.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T11:10:00Z
Subject: RE: Nexori pilot — operational feasibility notes

Quick operational read: we can support a 99.8% pilot SLO with these mandatory mitigations in the term sheet — otherwise we expose production customers to noisy fallouts. Required items:
- Scoped rollout (segment <= 5% of Nexori's production user base initially).
- KV/prefix caching enabled for the pilot traffic path to reduce token variance.
- Priority incident channel + weekly ops sync (1hr) with Nexori engineering.
- Telemetry: Live SLO dashboard with 15-minute granularity (shared view).

Risk: 99.8% materially increases probability of customer-visible incidents during peak; the credit cap needs to be paired with our ability to throttle or rollback quickly. If the commercial side wants 50% cap, we need explicit rollback permissions in the SOW and a two-week notice window for turning on broader protections.

Operationally OK to proceed with Marissa's proposed guardrails.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Product Manager, Platform Reliability
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Nexori pilot — final exec decision

Thanks for the tight summary and ops read. I approve moving forward with the pilot under the following executive conditions:

- Commercial: approve up to 30% one-time discount for the 90-day pilot.
- SLO deviation: allow 99.8% for pilot months only.
- Service credits cap: set at 40% of monthly hosting fees (not 50%).
- Mandatory guardrails: scoped rollout <=5% of Nexori's active users, live SLO dashboard (15-minute), weekly incident review, and an automated rollback trigger if incident rate breaches the agreed threshold for two consecutive weeks.
- Renewal/Conversion: require a renewal review meeting 30 days prior to pilot end to confirm whether to restore standard SLOs or renegotiate long-term terms; commercial discount will not auto-renew.

Marissa — please update the term sheet to reflect a 40% cap and send SOW redline to Nexori Legal. Avery — communicate the approved construct to Katie and confirm their go/no-go on the adjusted cap. Ben — include rollback and telemetry language in the ops annex.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
